title: Reservation tokens and blackout handshake for maintenance
creator: Diego Morales
description:
Problem: During planned maintenance (drains/upgrades) and autoscaler-driven resizes, we observe transient SLO violations when live requests lose preheated KV state or capacity unexpectedly drops. Current drain flow relies on simple out-of-band reservations and ad-hoc prewarm hooks but lacks a deterministic contract between fleet controller, autoscaler, and routing layers.

Proposal: Introduce a lightweight reservation token protocol and maintenance blackout handshake that lets an application-level throughput reservation be minted and consumed across the drain lifecycle. Tokens are ephemeral capacity reservations associated with a route/model pair and a maintenance epoch. They allow the routing layer to hold a bounded portion of capacity during disruptive operations and ensure KV prewarm (prefix caches) are preserved or warmed on replacement hosts before traffic moves.

Key components:
- Token minting service: integrated with fleet controller to issue reservation tokens when a maintenance window is scheduled or an autoscaling event is predicted. Tokens encode throughput units, TTL, model-version, and maintenance-epoch id.
- Handshake protocol: three-phase exchange (announce -> prewarm -> consume/transfer) between orchestrator, node agent, and router. Announce signals planned drain; prewarm requests KV snapshot transfer or lazy-warm hooks to target hosts; consume/transfer finalizes routing changes.
- Router integration: routing layer understands tokens and can hold reservation lanes; it enforces token-backed traffic shaping so that routes relying on tokens will not be evicted mid-request and will receive a prioritized fraction of burst capacity during the epoch.
- Autoscaler policy hooks: autoscaler will honor active tokens by scaling conservatively (preferred to scale-out rather than scale-in) until token expiry or explicit release.
- Observability & traces: expose token lifecycle in Console (per-token latency/cost breakouts), SLO hedging metrics (token-backed success rate), and a dedicated maintenance timeline trace in tracing UI.

Compatibility & safety:
- Backwards compatible: nodes that do not implement the agent will ignore tokens and fall back to existing drain semantics. Token adoption is opt-in per fleet.
- Fail-safe: token TTLs, circuit-breakers, and automatic release on controller loss to prevent stranded capacity.

Deliverables:
- API spec for minting/consuming tokens (gRPC + REST shim for Console)
- Node agent changes for prewarm snapshots and graceful drain hooks
- Router changes for token-aware traffic shaping
- Autoscaler policy extension to respect tokens
- Console UIs: maintenance timeline and per-token diagnostics
- E2E test harness & chaos tests (node reboot during prewarm, controller failover, token TTL expiry)

Success criteria:
- Reduce SLO violation rate during maintenance windows by >= 80% for instrumented routes in staging
- No more than 2% additional steady-state cost from reserved lanes in normal operations
- Feature gated rollout across Dedicated fleets with metrics and canary plan
